question: Comment: building fund
text:
Obviously the shul is ready to expand and this will cost a lot. However, the way the shul approached it seems unorganized and didn’t consider the financial situation of the community at large. Why is it that we haven’t seen one fundraising initiative outside of a large bill? 

There are many ways to fundraise and entice people to donate with events, dedications, and advertising. Asking for a SUGGESTED DONATION from members should be a last step after you already raised money, got people excited about the project, and know exactly how much you still need. People who can afford it will gladly pay extra to dedicate every door and bench. Those that are struggling won’t feel obligated to pay and will be more likely to donate if their situation improves. We may even donate our time or connections, if you don’t push us away. 

Donating to the shul is a choice that people make based on their financial capabilities. This is not a rich community. Many of the shul members can’t afford to own their own homes or struggle to pay a monthly mortgage. Even basic shul membership is a choice that is not easy to make. When we see a bill for the equivalent of 3 months rent on top of the membership we struggle to pay, it causes a lot of unnecessary anxiety, guilt and embarrassment. (Obviously we are obligated to pay this amount, but a unsettled bill still makes us feel like crap)
quote: People who can afford it will gladly pay extra to dedicate every door and bench.

I think the sanctuary should be wheelchair accessible. Obviously wouldn’t be an option for people to bring in strollers since there’s too many but inaccessibility is unfortunate. 

In the sanctuary, there’s no good spot for a kid who wants to sit on the floor to play quietly without blocking the aisles. I am a big proponent of my kids being in shul with me and don’t have anywhere to put them without being in the way of the bookcases or in the main walkway. (This was flagged by another member while my daughter was on the floor and I agree but don’t have a better option).

question: Comment: current building
text: This is related to some of the problems listed above, but I just want to frame it a different way. The main sanctuary used to be more equal in terms of space for women (the mechitza was closer to the Aron and the amud/shliach tzibur was therefore closer to the women's section). Understandably, as the men's section got more and more crowded, the mechitza was moved over. Even though I understand the reason for it, I wish there was a way to accommodate the number of men's seats needed while not making the women feel farther away. It makes it harder to hear Torah reading among other things.

text: We need a real beis midrash space. And I would like if the 8:15 maariv happened more often during the year.

question: Comment: current building
text: There needs to be a better and safer space for tot Shabbat. The room that it is in now is very unsafe for the many toddlers who are curious and could touch things they are not supposed to. There are exposed outlets, exposed brick, and very little space conducive for little kids. Also the nursing room needs to be better fitted. There is not enough space, the current door doesn’t close or lock very well and the bathroom doesn’t always work. Lastly, it would increase the shuls ability to have younger families become members if there was also a space for a mommy and me room that would be good for moms to hang out and talk and the kids too young for tot Shabbat to play. Currently this happens in the lobby which then creates crowding and noise issues. Also it could create a safety issue with so many people getting in and out of the lobby.

question: Comment: one improvement
text:
Looking at the categories above, I think there is a problem with making a distinction between prioritizing the main sanctuary and prioritizing the women's section. These ought to be the same thing, the same priority. 
At the same time, if Darchei is able to create flexible multipurpose spaces, that will provide space that can be used for youth purposes or for adult learning or small gathering spaces, which is why I listed that as a higher priority than specific rooms for specific things.

question: Comment: anything else
text:
I think accessibility is a place where the current building really falls short. Both in terms of access to important spaces for anyone with disabilities, and in terms of ease of getting out of the building safely in event of an emergency. A new building would be an opportunity to address that properly.
I hope that the design of the new sanctuary space takes women's experience of shul seriously, which requires making sure to speak to the women who come to shul consistently.
